holding.intro: Tanzania is rapidly becoming one of the most strategic investment hubs in Africa. Through its strong economic growth, expanding infrastructure, and access to regional markets, the country offers an excellent base for international investors seeking to structure and manage investments across Africa and globally.
holding.atPrimePost: , we specialize in assisting foreign investors, multinational groups, and global entrepreneurs in establishing Tanzania-based holding companies designed to control, manage, and expand international investments.
holding.definition: A holding company is a corporate entity created primarily to own shares, assets, and subsidiaries, allowing investors to manage multiple businesses under one centralized structure. This structure is widely used by global investment groups, multinational corporations, and high-net-worth individuals to manage cross-border investments efficiently.
holding.advantagesHeading: Why Global Investors Choose a Holding Company Structure
holding.advantagesIntro: A properly structured holding company provides several strategic advantages for international investors.
holding.adv1Desc: Own multiple businesses and investments through a single parent entity. This simplifies corporate governance and strategic decision-making while maintaining control across different markets.
holding.adv2Desc: Separate operational companies from the parent holding company to isolate risk and protect core assets from liabilities associated with individual businesses.
holding.adv3Desc: A holding company registered in Tanzania can legally own subsidiaries and assets in multiple jurisdictions, including companies in Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
holding.adv4Desc: As investors expand into new markets, additional subsidiaries can be added under the holding structure without restructuring the entire corporate group.
holding.diversificationDesc: Holding companies can manage a wide range of investments, including:
holding.tzHeading: Tanzania as a Strategic Investment Hub
holding.tzIntro: Tanzania provides several advantages for international investors establishing holding companies.
holding.tz1Desc: Access to more than 400 million consumers through regional economic blocs such as the East African Community (EAC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC).
holding.tz2Desc: Tanzania has maintained a stable political environment and consistent economic growth, making it an attractive destination for long-term investments.
holding.tz3Desc: Foreign investors can fully own companies in Tanzania, and corporate structures are flexible enough to support complex international investment strategies.
holding.tz4Desc: Located along the Indian Ocean, Tanzania serves as a key trade and logistics gateway connecting African markets with Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

fi.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
fi.faq.subtitle: Answers to common questions from foreign investors
fi.faq.q1: Can a foreign company own 100% of a Tanzanian company?
fi.faq.a1: Yes. Tanzania allows 100% foreign ownership in most sectors. Certain strategic sectors (mining, broadcast media) may require local equity participation. We will advise based on your specific sector.
fi.faq.q2: How long does company registration take in Tanzania?
fi.faq.a2: A standard LLC or subsidiary typically takes 3–5 weeks from submission of complete documents. A branch registration takes 4–6 weeks. Delays can occur at BRELA if documents are incomplete — we minimise this by preparing everything correctly upfront.
fi.faq.q3: Do I need to be physically present in Tanzania to register a company?
fi.faq.a3: No. Registration can be completed remotely with a Power of Attorney. However, corporate bank account opening may require at least one signatory to appear in person, depending on the bank.
fi.faq.q4: Does Tanzania accept Chinese Apostille documents?
fi.faq.a4: Tanzania joined the Hague Apostille Convention in 2020. China also joined in 2023. In principle, Chinese Apostille documents should be accepted. However, some government offices still request consular legalisation. We confirm the current requirement for each document type and government body before you incur any certification costs.
fi.faq.q5: What is the minimum share capital required?
fi.faq.a5: For a private limited company, there is no statutory minimum share capital in Tanzania. For foreign-owned companies registering with TIC (Tanzania Investment Centre) to access investment incentives, a minimum investment threshold of USD 500,000 applies.
fi.faq.q6: Can you assist with opening a bank account for a foreign-owned company?
fi.faq.a6: Yes. We work with CRDB Bank, NMB Bank, Stanbic, and Standard Chartered. We prepare the full KYC package and guide you through the process. Physical presence of at least one signatory is usually required by the bank.
fi.faq.q7: What taxes will my company pay in Tanzania?
fi.faq.a7: Corporate Income Tax (CIT): 30% of net profit. VAT: 18% on taxable supplies. Withholding Tax: varies by transaction type (5–15%). Companies in SEZ/EPZA may receive tax holidays of 5–10 years. We provide full tax planning as part of our annual compliance package.
fi.faq.q8: Do you offer services in Mandarin Chinese?
fi.faq.a8: Our inquiry form, key documents, and consultations are available in English and Mandarin. Our lead consultant has experience working with Chinese investors and construction companies. WhatsApp communication in Mandarin is welcome.
